title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right proximal posterior thigh just below the gluteal fold (subgluteal level), prone, under a transverse probe, as on ultrasound: medial on the image left, lateral on the right. Composition after NYSORA's subgluteal plate (Fig-6, concept only).
teachingPoint: Below the gluteal fold the sciatic nerve is a flat oval in the fascial plane under gluteus maximus, with biceps femoris medial and adductor magnus deep; the needle comes from lateral to its lateral edge and the spread surrounds it in the plane.
claims: Probe transverse just below the gluteal fold (record); the positioning plate shows the same level (owner, 2026-10-15).
Nerve deep to gluteus maximus (record), in the fascial plane between gluteus maximus, biceps femoris (medial) and adductor magnus (deep) (NYSORA subgluteal approach).
Long head of biceps femoris with its tendon medially; nerve in its own fascial sheath (standard anatomy; house style).
Needle in-plane from lateral to the lateral edge of the nerve (record: in-plane; NYSORA: lateral to medial).
Teal: spread around the nerve in the plane (record: inject around it).
Typical adult depths: nerve about 3.5 cm deep (schematic).
Labels: Gluteus maximus, Biceps femoris, Sciatic nerve, Adductor magnus.
